My reports about switching from Windows to Linux, mostly about software replacement
Good read. There is always an alternative application. People just have to be willing to look for and learn new things. Which sadly, most people are not.

I feel that's a little unfair. Sure, some are lazy and whatnot - but for some of us, it's a matter of time constraints.

Granted - most (read: almost all) applications have their equivalent on Linux - and a majority of those are so similar to their Windows counterpart (UI layout, workflow), that switching is a breeze.

But some of them are definitely not. And some of those take a really long time to master.

I code and do 3d work for a living - and while the coding is easily done on either Linux or Windows - the 3d stuff is what really gets to me.

Yea, I could learn Blender, but it would set me back a couple of years, and productivity would drop (Blender is fine - but I find the workflow gawd awful.. and Blender could never replace Z-Brush like the article suggests) - I might be stuck in my ways, but I'm pretty sure I'm not the only 'artist' with this problem.

If I was 14 again, and could start over - yea, I would have jumped on the OS bandwagon for sure. Not saying it is too late - it just becomes a lot more tedious and frustrating to switch at this point in life.
I feel it as well i dualboot one machine just for solidworks.

Quite a lot of this is very true, I've seen people let their desktop machine (no matter what kind it is) just sit and gather dust and when I ask them why doesn't their computer work they say something along the lines of "Oh I just use my tablet/phone now it's just to much of a trouble." Then I watch them fiddle with their portable device trying to get some webpage to load that isn't optimized for mobile what so ever. Yeah switching OS'es takes a lot of time and with more things you find yourself doing the more time it takes to get back into a workflow.

As for the Zbrush replacement I'm quite sure blender is not 100% on the level, currently all I do with it though is sculpt objects to 3D print figures for board games, every now and then I go crazy and make something large and detailed. Though I was using Zbrush to make perfectly tiled textures with bump mapping and specular ready to go so thats going to be the biggest jaw breaker to get over...or just dump several hours into getting it working on WINE...(hopes are not high at all)

As someone who is a professional in using the software they are using, yeah switching workflow just sounds like nightmare fuel to get over though I'm lucky enough that mostly everything (other than photos) are simply a hobby/rare commission so I'm taking advantage of that now.

Thank you for the article. Thank you for reminding people that there is always a productivity tool that does what someone needs.

if you want to find other software replacements, you may like http://alternativeto.net/?platform=linux

That site is quite helpful to get running right away but at times I feel there either isn't enough software that I've found on my own or as categorized quite well enough, such as finding a replacement for adobe bridge and it brings up darktable...not quite what I'd consider a proper replacement.

But it is very useful for the baby steps I was taking last year.
